assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new observational window opened by a very large instrument: a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos seen in a cubic-kilometre detector, then evidence for TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane. This is astroparticle physics at its core, and it rests on years of calibration and systematics work. I weigh the instrument and the discovery together.
assessment.attribution: Halzen drove the concept and the collaboration through AMANDA and IceCube, and Karle was a leading figure in detector construction and early analyses. Yoshida is credited but I judge his role less decisive. A discovery by a collaboration of several hundred is hard to assign to two or three people, and I am unsure of the internal division of leadership.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed in several independent channels (muon tracks, cascades, the Glashow-resonance event). The Galactic-plane result is newer. Timing looks right: the field is established and the instrument is mature, though identification of individual source classes is still developing.
uncertainties: Source identification beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 is still limited.
Fair credit across the collaboration and earlier AMANDA pioneers is unresolved.
I have not independently verified details of the most recent results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock and the magic-wavelength idea gave a measurement tool with fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It has changed precision metrology and fundamental tests, and it is a clean case of a new technique producing a new measurement capability. The result is clear and will last.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first strontium lattice clock. Ye brought the clocks to the 1e-18 level and developed the comparison and many-body work. A two-person prize is natural. Other clock groups are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have confirmed the clocks and compared them across laboratories. Recognition seems timely, and a redefinition of the second is under discussion.
uncertainties: Ye also appears in the ultracold molecules candidate, and the split against the earlier frequency-comb recognition is a matter for colleagues in atomic physics.
Whether the work is judged a distinct discovery or an extension of the earlier frequency-comb prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic peak is a standard ruler that now underpins dark-energy measurements through large galaxy surveys. The physics is simple and robust, and the 2005 detections were a landmark of observational cosmology. Early-universe theory and survey detection together make a lasting contribution.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein's SDSS luminous-red-galaxy detection and Cole's 2dFGRS detection are the two decisive measurements. Sunyaev (with Zeldovich, and independently Peebles and Yu in 1970) provided the theory. The credited set leaves out Peebles, already a laureate, and Yu, so the split between theory and observation is not straightforward.
assessment.maturity: The signal has been confirmed in many surveys (BOSS, eBOSS, 6dF, DESI) and is a mainstay of precision cosmology. Recent hints of evolving dark energy remind us the interpretation can change, but the ruler itself is secure.
uncertainties: Credit for the 1970 theory is split among people not all in the credited list.
Whether the committee wants more cosmology after the 2011 and 2019 prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray and optical afterglows settled the distance scale of gamma-ray bursts and showed they are cosmological, which led to the link with supernovae and black-hole formation. It is a decisive observational result obtained with a space instrument, the kind of work I know well.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228. Kulkarni led the redshift, radio and optical follow-up. This is a reasonable three-way split, but the optical and redshift contributions (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger and others) make attribution contested, and I am not certain who should be included.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed many times over by Swift, Fermi and other missions in the last 25 years. If anything, recognition is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit among the optical and redshift teams is disputed.
Eligibility may be limited if some key people are deceased; I am not certain who.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics is the basis of readout and control in superconducting quantum processors, and the strong-coupling experiment was original and clear. The impact is wide. I lean on colleagues in quantum information for the deeper assessment, but the instrument-like quality of the work, a designed microwave cavity coupled to a qubit, appeals to me.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the experiments by Wallraff and Schoelkopf share the credit. Wallraff and Schoelkopf led the experiments and Blais carried the central theory. Girvin is also a strong claim, and four credited names do not fit a prize of three, so there is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and extended by many independent laboratories and widely used. Timing is delicate because the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and the committee might want some distance.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize and whether a second circuit-based prize is wanted so soon.
Choice between Blais and Girvin as the theory recipient.
Outside my expertise in quantum information.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have given evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, opening a new window on supermassive black-hole binaries or early-universe sources. Measuring the Hellings-Downs correlation is a very difficult precision-timing experiment resting on long, careful systematics work.
assessment.attribution: The credited names are leaders of the main arrays and of the pulsar-timing programme. This is a plausible set, but the discovery is the work of very large collaborations, and the founding contributions (Hellings and Downs, Detweiler, Foster and Backer, Sazhin) lie outside it.
assessment.maturity: Premature in my view. The 2023 results were individually at roughly 2 to 4 sigma, the combined IPTA analysis is still in progress, and the source (binaries versus new physics) is not identified. I would want a clear 5-sigma detection and independent confirmation first.
uncertainties: The significance of the signal may be below the usual discovery threshold.
The origin of the background is not settled.
Credit among collaborations and early proponents is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a field of moire materials, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable system. Prediction and experiment fit together unusually well, and the impact on condensed matter is large. This is outside my own expertise and I would defer to the condensed-matter colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the devices and found the correlated phases in 2018. Junior team members who made key measurements are not credited. A theorist plus experimentalist pairing is the natural configuration among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated and the field is moving fast. The timing is possible but may be early for a final judgement.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
Credit for experimental team members is not in the credited list.
Beyond my direct expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres gave a room-temperature solid-state quantum sensor, with uses from nanoscale magnetometry to biology. It is an instrument-driven advance that I value, and it opened a measurement capability that did not exist before.
assessment.attribution: The Wrachtrup group showed optical detection of single NV centres in 1997, and Jelezko and Wrachtrup demonstrated coherent control in 2004. Lukin is credited for the quantum-register and sensing work and could fit as a third name, but I prefer the two who established basic detection and control. Other groups outside the credited list (for example Hanson, Awschalom) may have a claim.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories confirm and use the technique, and the applications are real. Timing is acceptable, though the committee could judge it more technology than discovery.
uncertainties: Competition with other candidates in quantum technology.
Whether Lukin or others should be included.
Solid-state and quantum-information aspects are outside my expertise.
